title: Versal formal objects map to every formal object
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $l$ a field finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-field, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Use the test category, predeformation categories, formal objects and versality of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a predeformation category on $\mathcal C_{R,l}$. All complete local algebras below are Noetherian, are complete for their maximal ideals, and have specified residue field $l$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. A morphism from a formal object $\alpha$ over $A$ to $\beta$ over $B$ consists of a local residue-preserving $R$-map $f:A\to B$ and compatible isomorphisms between the evaluations of $\alpha$ along $A\to B/\mathfrak m_B^n$ and $\beta_n$, for every $n\geq1$. Let $\xi$ over $C$ be versal. Then for every formal object $\eta$ over $D$, there exists a morphism $\xi\to\eta$; in particular its underlying map $C\to D$ is a local residue-preserving $R$-map.

proof.text: Put $D_n=D/\mathfrak m_D^n$ for $n\geq1$ and let $q_n:D_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow D_n$ be the quotient. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] to $D$, $K=\mathfrak m_D^n$ and $N=n$: $D_n$ is Artinian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_D/\mathfrak m_D^n$. Its residue field is the specified $l$, so $D_n\in\mathcal C_{R,l}$ and $q_n$ is a surjective morphism there. Write $t_n:(q_n)_*\eta_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\eta_n$ for the given transitions.

source.place: Tag 06HT (lemma-versal-object-quasi-initial), expanding the successive-lifting proof of Tag 06HN (lemma-smooth-morphism-essentially-surjective), with Tag 06HS (remark-versal-object)

proof.text: We construct local residue-preserving maps $a_n:C\to D_n$ and isomorphisms $u_n:\xi_{D_n,a_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\eta_n$ by recursion, with $q_na_{n+1}=a_n$ and $t_n\circ(q_n)_*u_{n+1}=u_n$ after the evaluation comparisons. For $n=1$, take $a_1$ to be $C\to l\cong D_1$. The predeformation condition gives the unique isomorphism $u_1$ in the fibre over $l$. Here $\xi_{D_n,a_n}$ denotes evaluation as defined in [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category].

source.place: Tag 06HT (lemma-versal-object-quasi-initial), expanding the successive-lifting proof of Tag 06HN (lemma-smooth-morphism-essentially-surjective), with Tag 06HS (remark-versal-object)

proof.text: Given $(a_n,u_n)$, apply the defining versality lifting property to $D_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow D_n$, $a_n$, $y=\eta_{n+1}$ and the specified isomorphism $u_n^{-1}\circ t_n:(q_n)_*\eta_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\xi_{D_n,a_n}$. It supplies a local residue-preserving lift $a_{n+1}$ and an isomorphism $v:\eta_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\xi_{D_{n+1},a_{n+1}}$ extending this specified isomorphism. Set $u_{n+1}=v^{-1}$. The extension equation gives $t_n\circ(q_n)_*u_{n+1}=u_n$ under the fixed evaluation comparisons. Choosing one such lift at each recursion step produces the compatible sequence; no uniqueness of these lifts is asserted.

source.place: Tag 06HT (lemma-versal-object-quasi-initial), expanding the successive-lifting proof of Tag 06HN (lemma-smooth-morphism-essentially-surjective), with Tag 06HS (remark-versal-object)

proof.text: For $x\in C$, the tuple $(a_n(x))_{n\geq1}$ is compatible. By the definition of completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and completeness of $D$, it is the image of a unique element $a(x)\in D$. Componentwise operations and the injectivity of $D\to\varprojlim_nD_n$ show that $a:C\to D$ is a unital $R$-algebra map, with reduction $a_n$ for every $n$. Its residue map is the identity because this holds for $a_1$; hence $a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)=\mathfrak m_C$, so $a$ is local. In particular $a(\mathfrak m_C^n)\subseteq\mathfrak m_D^n$.

source.place: Tag 06HT (lemma-versal-object-quasi-initial), expanding the successive-lifting proof of Tag 06HN (lemma-smooth-morphism-essentially-surjective), with Tag 06HS (remark-versal-object)

proof.text: The evaluation of $\xi$ along $C\xrightarrow{a}D\to D_n$ is exactly $\xi_{D_n,a_n}$, with the fixed higher-level comparisons of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Thus the $u_n$ are the required evaluation isomorphisms. Their adjacent compatibility was imposed in the recursion; compatibility for arbitrary $m\geq n$ follows by composing the adjacent equalities, using the transport associativity axiom. Therefore $(a,(u_n)_n)$ is the morphism $\xi\to\eta$ described in the statement.
